items.title: Borno settles N622m NECO fees for 27,599 students – Commissioner
items.description: The Borno government has settled N622.3 million for 27,599 students sitting for the National Examinations Council (NECO) for the 2026 Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) in public schools. Mr Lawan Wakilbe, the state Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation, announced this while presenting the cheque to NECO officials on Friday in Maiduguri. Wakilbe said the payment was part of the state government’s commitment to ensuring that no child was denied access to education or external examinations because of financial constraints. He said the government has, since 2019, consistently subsidised 75 per cent of examination fees for eligible students sitting for the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), SSCE. “National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examinations,” he said. According to him, the N622.3 million covers the 2026 NECO SSCE examination fees for 27,599 public school students across the state. He said the government had also committed N1.195 billion in 2026 to WASSCE, SSCE, State Islamic Studies Examination (SISE) and NABTEB examinations. Wakilbe said the state government had invested N5.987 billion in external examination fees since the commencement of the intervention in 2019. He added that the investment had benefited 193,396 students across the state. The commissioner said the 2026 SSCE was conducted in 24 Local Government Areas despite security challenges confronting some communities. He, however, expressed concern over the abduction of 36 learners and a teacher during a security incident at Lassa on June 29, while the examination was ongoing. Wakilbe prayed for the safe return of the abducted persons and commended NECO officials, local government chairmen, and education secretaries. “Principals, teachers, parents and other stakeholders for contributing to the successful conduct of the examination,” he said The post Borno settles N622m NECO fees for 27,599 students – Commissioner appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AfriYAN Ghana calls for greater youth participation in local governance
items.description: The African Youth and Adolescents Network on Population and Development (AfriYAN Ghana) has called for greater youth participation in local governance and the integration of young people’s priorities into district development plans and budgets. The call was made at a stakeholder dialogue organised by LoveAid Foundation under AfriYAN Ghana, in partnership with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), in the Volta Region. The dialogue brought together representatives of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), civil society organisations and youth groups to explore practical ways of incorporating young people’s views into local development planning and budgeting. Participants agreed that youth priorities should be progressively incorporated into the Medium-Term Development Plans and annual budgets of assemblies to ensure that identified needs are properly funded and implemented. Speaking to the media after the event, Programmes Officer of LoveAid Foundation, Joshua Tettey Ayayi, said the dialogue formed part of the organisation’s Adolescent Girls Project, which seeks to educate and empower adolescent girls to protect themselves against gender-based and sexual violence while strengthening youth participation in governance. “What we convened here is to ensure that the inputs of young people are incorporated into development plans, budgeted for, and fully implemented.” Mr Ayayi said meaningful youth participation in decision-making was essential to sustainable community development and ensuring that policies and programmes reflected the actual needs of young people. Assemblies urged to strengthen youth engagement The Presiding Member of the Akatsi North District Assembly, Patrick Kwame Ahiabu, also called on district assemblies to strengthen youth engagement through their Public Relations and Complaints Committees (PRCCs). He said the PRCC, which serves as a communication link between assemblies and their constituents, was not functioning effectively in many districts due to inadequate funding. “We have realised that the assembly is not adequately involving the youth through the PRCC. The PRCC is the mouthpiece of the district assembly. Unfortunately, this committee is not functioning effectively in most assemblies.” Mr Ahiabu said assemblies must make adequate budgetary allocations to the committees to enable them to effectively engage communities on government projects and other development initiatives. “When we prepare our budgets, we need to make adequate allocations to the PRCC so that it can effectively advocate and sensitise communities on government projects,” he added. He said adequately resourcing the PRCC would improve public education and transparency while creating more opportunities for young people to participate in local governance. Focus on adolescent girls The stakeholder dialogue also formed part of efforts to protect the rights and wellbeing of adolescent girls. Through the Adolescent Girls Project, LoveAid Foundation seeks to educate and empower girls to protect themselves against gender-based and sexual violence while creating platforms for young people to contribute to decisions affecting their communities. AfriYAN Ghana, the Ghana chapter of the continental African Youth and Adolescents Network on Population and Development, is a youth-led organisation focused on the health, rights and wellbeing of young people. The organisation works with development partners, including UNFPA, on issues such as meaningful youth participation in governance, sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender equality, leadership development and youth empowerment. Through advocacy, capacity building and community engagement, AfriYAN Ghana seeks to ensure that young people have a meaningful role in shaping policies and programmes that affect their lives.

items.title: Journée de l’Excellence scolaire 2026 : Le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ aux jeunes lauréats : « science, science et science, tout est science ! Cherchez la connaissance scientifique et technologique »
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a salué, ce vendredi 4 septembre 2026, le mérite des meilleurs élèves et enseignants à l'occasion de la Journée de l'Excellence Scolaire (JES), édition 2026. Loin des hommages académiques conventionnels, le Chef de l'État a exhorté la jeunesse burkinabè à une rupture avec la résignation religieuse et à un virage vers les disciplines scientifiques et techniques. Le Camarade Président du Faso et les deux meilleurs enseignants de l'année scolaire 2026 Abordant d’emblée ce qu'il qualifie de sujets « sensibles mais nécessaires », le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a vivement dénoncé le détournement de la religion à des fins de domination. Citant le célèbre Homme d'État kenyan Jomo KENYATTA, le Capitaine TRAORÉ a rappelé comment la colonisation et l’emprise idéologique ont dépossédé les Africains de leurs richesses. Il a appelé les Africains à cesser de rejeter la responsabilité des échecs humains sur le divin : « Un être qui n'est pas utile à sa communauté est un ennemi de Dieu. Tant que vous ne vous battez pas, Dieu ne vous accompagne pas ». Les lauréats de l'éducation inclusive ont également reçu leurs récompenses des mains du Camarade Président du Faso L'urgence de l'industrialisation et l'impératif des filières scientifiques Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a invité les lauréats à s’inscrire dans une dynamique de créativité pour accompagner le développement du Burkina Faso Pour le Chef de l'État, la souveraineté économique du Burkina Faso ne pourra s'articuler qu'autour d'une transformation profonde de la jeunesse et de l'appareil éducatif. Il a réaffirmé la détermination du gouvernement à procéder à une réorientation massive dès la rentrée scolaire prochaine, vers des filières scientifiques et le recrutement massif d'enseignants spécialisés pour pallier le manque de compétences techniques sur le marché national. Ils sont au total 188 lauréats, élèves et enseignants, qui ont été recompensés cette année pour leurs résultats scolaires En effet, sur environ 65 000 bacheliers, plus de 50% sont de la série littéraire, alors que les séries scientifiques et industrielles ne comptent respectivement que 571 pour le BAC série C et 38 lauréats pour le BAC série E. « On ne se construira jamais comme cela », a averti le Président du Faso. « L’africain qui n’est pas capable de se nourrir, qu’il meure ! » S'adressant à l'ensemble des dirigeants africains et à la conscience collective du continent, le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire a dénoncé le drame de la migration clandestine et l'assistanat international. « L’africain qui n’est pas capable de se nourrir, qu’il meure ! On doit être en mesure de produire, on a assez de terres ici. Pourquoi c'est nous qui devons aller mendier ailleurs ? », regrette-t-il. La Journée de l'Excellence Scolaire 2026, célébrée sous le thème « Cultiver l’excellence scolaire dans le contexte de la refondation de l’école burkinabè », a été parrainée par le président de la Fondation Bank of Africa (BOA), le camarade Lassiné DIAWARA et le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO. Le représentant des parrains, Camarade Lassiné DIAWARA a soutenu que l’excellence scolaire transcende les résultats scolaires pour se déteindre sur la personnalité des lauréats Pour eux, l'excellence dépasse le cadre des résultats scolaires immédiats, elle s'inscrit dans un état d'esprit durable soutenu par la discipline et l'intégrité. « Les diplômes ouvrent des portes, mais c'est le caractère qui les maintient ouvertes. Le talent crée des opportunités, mais c'est le travail qui assure un succès durable », indique le parrain Lassiné DIAWARA. Le porte-parole des lauréats, le camarade Sékou TRAORÉ, a salué l'effort du Gouvernement à refonder le système éducatif en misant sur l'innovation, la rigueur et l'enseignement technique. Il a exprimé sa gratitude aux éducateurs, avec une mention spéciale à ceux qui sont dans les zones à fort défi sécuritaire, aux encadreurs et aux Forces combattantes. Selon Sékou TRAORÉ, le prix de l’excellence n’est pas un accomplissement final, mais un devoir de servir la Nation avec intégrité, compétence et créativité. Direction de la Communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Sécurité : La 45e Promotion de l’ENP célèbre une décennie d’engagement au service de la Patrie
items.description: La 45e promotion de l'École Nationale de Police a entamé ce vendredi 4 septembre 2026, la célébration de ses dix ans de service. Pendant 48 heures, la promotion baptisée « Professionnalisme et engagement Patriotique » aura l'occasion de se remémorer leur parcours, de se recentrer sur leurs valeurs et de renouveler leur serment envers la Nation. Pour joindre l'utile à l'agréable, la 45e Promotion a offert 7,5 tonnes de riz, 140 bidons d'huile de 5 litres ainsi que des kits de savon détergent aux veuves et orphelins des camarades tombés sur le champ d'honneur. La célébration est Placée sous le haut patronage du Commissaire divisionnaire de police Mahamadou Sana, ministre de la Sécurité, et présidée par l'Inspecteur général de police Thierry Dofizouho Tuina, Directeur général de la police nationale, cette commémoration de deux jours revêt une signification toute particulière pour les membres de cette promotion baptisée « Professionnalisme et engagement Patriotique ». Il y a 10 ans sortait de la cuvée de l'École nationale de police, une promotion qui ne fut pas un simple complément d'effectif, mais des professionnels engagés pour la défense de la patrie. Le Presidium de la cérémonie d'ouverture. Le directeur général de la Police nationale (au fond). Le Dircab, représentant le ministre de la sécurité (au milieu). Le Commissaire Kafando représentant le parrain (à l'extrême droite) Baptisée « Professionnalisme et engagement Patriotique », cette 45e promotion a, selon le Commissaire divisionnaire de police Wendinmanegdé Emmanuel Zongo, Directeur de Cabinet représentant le ministre de la Sécurité, fait honneur à la patrie. Le représentant du ministre de la Sécurité a tenu à saluer le parcours accompli par ces policiers qui ont su faire face à un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement difficile. « Dix ans, c'est un parcours fait de réussite et de difficulté et des défis à relever », a-t-il souligné, avant d'ajouter que « globalement la promotion a fait ce qu'elle pouvait dans un contexte difficile. Elle a donné le meilleur d'elle-même ». Wendinmanegdé Emmanuel Zongo saluant les résultats de cette 45e promotion Tout en reconnaissant les difficultés rencontrées, notamment « le risque de l'individualisme », le Directeur de Cabinet a lancé un appel solennel à la promotion pour « rester intellectuellement vivant, unis, solidaires, parce que le chemin est encore long. Une vingtaine d'années pour la majorité reste à faire. Nous leur souhaitons une belle carrière, une carrière réussie pour le bonheur du Burkina Faso ». Cette décennie de service n'a pourtant pas été de tout repos pour ces hommes et ces femmes qui ont œuvré sur tous les fronts, comme l'a rappelé le Commissaire principal de police Sié Ibrahim Ouattara, président du Comité d'organisation. « 10 ans plus tard nous avons connu les difficultés du métier, ses satisfactions et ses sacrifices. Nous avons servi avec dévouement et engagement. Nous étions partout, nous étions sur le champ de combat, dans l'administration, nous sommes toujours dans l'administration, nous sommes toujours sur le champ du combat, nous serons toujours sur le champ du combat », a-t-il déclaré. Le Commissaire Ouattara galvanisant ses camarades pour les nouveaux défis à relever Au-delà des retrouvailles et de la fraternité, cette célébration a également été marquée par un geste de solidarité envers les familles des camarades disparus. « En marge de la célébration de nos 10 ans de carrière, nous avons fait un don de 7,5 tonnes de riz, 140 bidons d'huile de 5 litres, des kits de savon détergent d'une entreprise locale. Nous avons tenu à faire ce don pour accompagner les veuves et les orphelins des camarades tombés sur le champ d'honneur », a précisé le président du comité d'organisation. L'événement a également été marqué par la présence du Commissaire divisionnaire de police Émile Kafando, représentant le parrain, le Contrôleur général de police Edmond Tapsoba. Remise de don aux veuves et enfants des camarades tombés sur le champ de bataille Le programme des 48 heures de célébration comprend, outre les actions humanitaires et le don de sang, des activités sportives telles qu'un cross populaire suivi d'un match de football opposant la 45e promotion à leurs formateurs, ainsi que des conférences. La promotion prévoit également de faire don de matériels didactiques à l'École nationale de police et de matériel symbolique à l'AS Police. La journée de samedi 5 septembre 2026 sera consacrée à une assemblée générale permettant aux promotionnaires de « se parler sans la hiérarchie, voir ce qui a marché, ce qui n'a pas marché et ce qui doit être fait », selon le président du comité d'organisation. Il faut préciser que la majorité des membres de cette promotion abordent le premier tiers de leur carrière. « Aujourd'hui nous sommes pour la majorité à 1/3 des années de notre carrière. On ne peut que dire merci à Dieu, merci à l'institution policière et également interpeller nos promotionnaires à un engagement renouvelé. Nos 10 ans sont passés mais le reste des années à venir pourrait être plus dur. C'est interpeller chacun à la mobilisation générale », a conclu le Commissaire principal Sié Ibrahim Ouattara. Un aperçu de l'assistance à la cérémonie d'ouverture En guise d'information, la célébration des 10 ans de la 45e promotion est placée sous le thème : « « Dix ans d’engagement au service de la Patrie : mémoire, introspection et serment renouvelé ». Lire aussi : Sécurité : La Police nationale renforce le leadership de ses nouveaux directeurs Mathias KAM Minute.bf

items.title: Ouahbi et Sacramento soutiennent Rahimi après le décès de son père
items.description: Le sélectionneur national Mohamed Ouahbi a tenu à apporter son soutien à Soufiane Rahimi après le décès de son père, Mohamed Rahimi, plus connu sous le surnom de « Youari », figure emblématique du Raja Casablanca. Accompagné de son adjoint João Sacramento, le sélectionneur des Lions de l’Atlas a été aperçu dans une séquence relayée sur les réseaux sociaux alors qu’il se préparait à se rendre auprès de la famille Rahimi pour lui présenter ses condoléances. Une démarche qui a été largement saluée par les supporters marocains. وهبي ومساعده ساكرامنتو يحضران لتقديم التعازي في وفاة "يوعري" #الرجاء_الرياضي #يوعري #البطولة pic.twitter.com/tPZQS4HTTf — Elbotola – البطولة (@elbotola) September 4, 2026 Le père de Soufiane Rahimi est décédé jeudi. Pendant plusieurs décennies, il avait occupé la fonction de responsable des équipements du Raja, côtoyant plusieurs générations de joueurs, d’entraîneurs et de dirigeants du club casablancais. Le Raja lui a rendu hommage, saluant la mémoire d’un homme dont le nom était étroitement associé à l’histoire des Verts et à la vie quotidienne du club. Sur le plan sportif, Soufiane Rahimi poursuit actuellement son aventure avec Al-Ain. L’international marocain a déjà disputé trois rencontres cette saison, toutes comme titulaire, avec deux buts et une passe décisive. The post Ouahbi et Sacramento soutiennent Rahimi après le décès de son père appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: MTN Ghana, University of Ghana seal pact to Drive Digital Future.
items.description: MTN Ghana Chief Executive Officer, Stephen Blewitt, says the company’s new partnership with the University of Ghana is aimed at bridging academia and industry to position Ghana as the epicenter of global digital innovation. Speaking at the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with the University, Mr. Blewitt described the collaboration as a natural alliance between two powerful institutions. “It is a great institution with a great history of moving Ghana forward, and that is an important part of why we want to work with you,” he said. He noted that the partnership, which began as a discussion months ago, has matured into a concrete step to support Ghana’s digital growth. This meeting is a step forward in strengthening the bridge between academia and industry. When you put together a powerful digital company like MTN and a powerful academic institution like UG, you can give birth to amazing things,” he stated. Mr. Blewitt highlighted Ghana’s immense talent at home and abroad, stressing the need to drive digital transformation beyond tech into agri-tech and infrastructure. He said Artificial Intelligence is no longer optional. “AI is upon us. AI cannot be ignored. Even if you think you don’t need AI, AI is somewhere touching your life. We need to, as a country, lead our own destiny when it comes to AI,” he said. The MTN CEO praised UG for shaping future leaders, noting that the world’s greatest innovations often started as small ideas in university dormitories. He announced a hackathon under the partnership to move ideas from theory to practice. I like hackathons because they bring theory to practice. We have a problem; we need to find a solution,” he said, adding that the initiative will go beyond ideas to mentorship, incubation, pilots and real-world deployment. Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana, Prof. Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, said the partnership is critical to preparing students for a rapidly changing world of work. “These two worlds cannot operate separately,” she said, noting that MTN operates daily at the frontier of technology. Prof. Amfo said transformative student experience is UG’s first strategic priority and goes beyond lectures. “The real test is whether the education they receive prepares them for the world of work. That world is changing rapidly as AI, data analytics and digital platforms change jobs and business models,” she said. She disclosed that UG is reviewing its Required Courses to introduce compulsory modules in digital literacy, applied AI, gender equality, disability and inclusion. Chief Digital Officer of MTN Ghana, Ibrahim Misto, said Ghana’s youth must lead the AI revolution, not just consume it. “Today we are making a clear statement that Ghana’s young people must not simply consume the AI revolution; they must help build it, shape it and lead it,” he said. The (Tɛkyerɛma Pa) AI Hackathon 2026, part of MTN’s 30th anniversary celebration under the theme “30 Years of Progress, Power to You,” aligns with MTN’s focus on connectivity, fintech and digital infrastructure. “At MTN, we believe technology creates value only when it creates impact,” Misto said, urging students to “build for impact, not applause,” with solutions relevant to Ghana, scalable across Africa, and competitive globally.

items.title: Give time some time
items.description: If you say you love someone, time will tell. If you say you badly need them in your life, time always has a way of telling whether you mean it or not. Time will test whether it is love… or just some passing desire. We will always need to pass life’s test of time! Time has power. Like a prophet, it will let the world know why we do what we do. If you say you love me, only time will tell. If you say till death do us part, only time will tell if poverty will not put a wedge between us. The good times will come. The bad times will come, too. Whether we loved others for who they are or what they have, only time will tell. Whether our love for others is one birthed out of a genuine heart or a selfish one, let’s leave it for time to tell. Time never lies. It will always uncover the truth, no matter how well we have covered it with well-calculated lies. Time will test our intentions. It will test our character. If you want to know whether a man means what he says to you, give it [him] time. When a woman promises you she can go to the moon and back just for your sake, give it [her] time. When someone says they love you from the depth of their soul, only time can ever tell. Time will make them decide. Time will make them choose you over others if they truly love you. Love that hasn’t been time-tested is no love yet. When someone tells you they love you, nod… and let time do the answering. Love is like walking into a restaurant. Ordering food is free. Getting it delivered to your table, however, comes at a cost. Making all the promises to your partner is free. Walking up the aisle to swear in the eyes of the public comes at almost no cost. Living by those promises, however, does. It comes at a price to love! When you love someone, you do what you say. When you do not, you only say what you are supposed to do. When you truly love them, you are ready to give up your comfort for their sake. When you are only taking them for a ride, you are ready to take their comfort even for your own sake! Time will test whether our love is selfish. Time will always tell. When a couple is all excited about putting a ring on each other’s finger, only one person can tell whether they’d still have each other’s back when the scales of love have fallen off their eyes time. Time is a timeless prophet! The love we have for others will definitely be tested. What we feel for them will pass through the furnace of time. Indeed, time will expose every hidden desire inside of us. Time can reveal the good and bad intentions inside us. Hard times will try to get in the way of our love. Our personal differences will do the same. Time will tell whether our love for others is an empty promise. If you say you love someone, give it time. If someone says they love you, give it time. Love may grow old, but it should never grow cold. Despite all the reasons time throws at us to give up on those we love, we ought to still make that conscious effort to water the field of love we have for them. Love is action, a voluntary action. Love is not conjured from the skies. We create it. True love is making an effort to stay with our loved ones, even in the bad times. When all the odds are against us, time will test our promises. When our partners lose their jobs, time will test whether our love for them will vanish all of a sudden. Our loved ones will age. They may put on weight. They will not always be who they are physically, but time will test our love for them emotionally. Time will always test our love. Time will always test the genuineness of our hearts and minds. Between what we say and what we do is a bridge called time. It will always tell whether we mean what we say. It will always tell whether we spoke from our heads… or our hearts. So… when that gentleman is all excited about you, do not be too excited. Give him time. When that young lady is all over you every minute, exercise a little more patience. It may not always be love. It may not always be what we assume it should be. We may have many questions on our minds. However, like an examiner of life, time always has the answers. Time will always expose the motivation behind what we do. If you love her, time will tell. If you love him, time will tell, too. No one knows our thoughts until time gives them away. We may deceive others with our words, but time will definitely expose our actions. Let love lead. Only time can tell what will ever have the lead in our lives.

items.title: Non, Mamadou Hawa Gassama n’est pas décédé
items.description: Une publication annoncant le deces de l'ancien depute malien Mamadou Hawa Gassama circule sur les reseaux sociaux depuis le 29 août. Apres verification, cette information est fausse. Contacte par notre redaction, l'ancien elu affirme etre en bonne sante et dement cette rumeur. La publication largement partagee sur les reseaux sociaux annonce depuis le 29 août le deces de l'ancien depute Mamadou Awa Gassama. Selon cette publication, l'ancien elu serait decede a l'Hopital du Mali. L'information a ete relayee sur les reseaux sociaux sans qu'aucune source officielle ne vienne la confirmer. Gassama dement la rumeur Pour verifier cette information, la redaction a contacte directement Mamadou Hawa Gassama. L'ancien depute dement categoriquement l'annonce de son deces. « Je suis en parfaite sante », affirme-t-il, precisant ne souffrir « meme pas d'une petite migraine ». a la suite de la diffusion de cette fausse information, Mamadou Awa Gassama a egalement publie une video dans laquelle il dement la rumeur. Une fausse information largement relayee Le contact direct avec monsieur Gassama et la video publiee par l'ancien elu permettent de conclure que cette information est totalement fausse. Cette nouvelle intox rappelle les risques lies au partage rapide d'informations non verifiees sur les reseaux sociaux. Les annonces de deces sont particulierement sensibles. Avant de les relayer, il est recommande d'en verifier l'origine, de rechercher une confirmation aupres de proches ou de sources fiables et, lorsque cela est possible, de contacter directement la personne concernee. Lire aussi : Pourquoi les rumeurs circulent elles si vite sur WhatsApp ? L’article Non, Mamadou Hawa Gassama n’est pas décédé est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Sudan Nashra: Hemedti in Addis Ababa | Buildup at Ethiopian base fuels concerns over RSF corridor toward Blue Nile capital, military sends massive reinforcements | RSF fortifies West Darfur capital with berms, reinforces troops | RSF commander in North Kordofan defects, arrives in capital with 200 fighters
items.description: Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . When Rapid Support Forces Commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo quietly touched down in Addis Ababa last week, the Blue Nile State front was raging along Ethiopia’s border and reinforcements for the fighting were amassing on both sides. Ethiopia, meanwhile, was contending with renewed tensions of its own. For the RSF, keeping channels open with Addis Ababa is particularly important given that its border is part of the security environment surrounding the fighting in Blue Nile. Operations and troop movements along the border were among the main subjects of Hemedti’s talks, according to an RSF leadership source and an Ethiopian government source who spoke to Mada Masr. For the Ethiopian source, Addis Ababa’s immediate concern is keeping Sudan’s war from spilling across the border. But Sudanese intelligence sees another layer to Ethiopia’s interest in the RSF. Ethiopia could factor the paramilitary group into its own military arrangements as it manages conflicts with domestic opponents, particularly amid renewed tensions with Tigray, a Sudanese intelligence source said. Such a relationship could also give Addis Ababa greater room to operate on the Sudanese side of the border, they added. The Sudanese military is watching that possibility from an increasingly exposed position. It has lost the strategic border towns of Geisan and Kurmuk in Blue Nile and is now trying to stop the advance from the border toward Blue Nile’s capital, Damazin. And there is a new reason for concern — a significant buildup since July at an Ethiopian military base in Asosa, located in the Benishangul-Gumuz region bordering Sudan. The area has been repeatedly used to launch major operations by the RSF and its allies into Blue Nile. But an intelligence source in the state said the recent buildup could make the cross-border corridor into Kurmuk and Geisan harder for the military to penetrate and could facilitate the unimpeded movement of supplies and forces to the RSF and its allies. With the border towns secured, the RSF and its allies are now pushing against the military positions guarding Damazin. They captured Bakori in the Geisan locality and Sirkum in Kurmuk last week, triggering a rush of military reinforcements into the state capital and the positions around it. While the military is shoring up Damazin, the RSF is fortifying Geneina, the capital of West Darfur. Military operations this week secured another position near the city, part of an offensive that has been underway since July and has brought military and allied forces within reach of the RSF-held capital. The RSF is now digging around the city, extending sand berms and trenches as a defensive measure against a possible surprise attack. This week, it brought in large numbers of fighters in what a military field source described as preparation for attacks on military positions in West Darfur and neighboring North Darfur. Kordofan, the war’s critical faultline between an RSF push east and a military push west, saw its second major defection this week. Abu Bakr Dahloub, the RSF’s intelligence chief for special missions in North Kordofan’s Hamra al-Sheikh and the Egypt-Libya-Sudan border triangle, defected to the military with around 200 fighters. After securing major gains in North Kordofan weeks ago, the military continues to target RSF supply and gathering points in neighboring West Kordofan. Military aircraft struck several fuel and ammunition depots and RSF gatherings there this week, destroying supplies that had just arrived to reinforce positions in the area. In Khartoum, the state is trying to get its internal political dialogue off the ground despite intractable disagreements with major political forces over the process itself. The dialogue’s preparatory committee announced its formation this week and is now beginning outreach. But ongoing disputes over the committee’s independence, the fact that talks will be held in military-controlled territory and the question of who gets a seat at the table remain major obstacles to its efforts to secure participation. *** Hemedti in Addis Ababa In his second trip to the Ethiopian capital since the war broke out, RSF Commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo arrived in Addis Ababa in an unannounced visit on August 26. Hemedti’s first visit, in December 2023, was a formal trip that culminated in a political declaration with Abdalla Hamdok, the prime minister he had ousted with his once-ally Sudanese military chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. His quiet return comes as the Ethiopia-Sudan border figures directly in the fighting, while Khartoum and Addis Ababa accuse each other of backing forces in the other’s conflict. A source in the RSF leadership said Hemedti met with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, but an Ethiopian government source informed of the contacts neither confirmed nor denied that the two had met, saying only that Hemedti met with Ethiopian officials. Both sources said the stated purpose of the visit was to discuss political developments, prospects for peace and the course of the war. But the fighting and growing security concerns along the Sudan-Ethiopia border occupied much of the discussions, according to the two sources as well as a source in Sudan’s General Intelligence Service who spoke to Mada Masr. According to the intelligence source, the visit could mark a point at which Addis Ababa begins factoring the RSF into its own military calculations around its internal conflicts, particularly the renewed tensions with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front. For the RSF leadership, maintaining contact with the Ethiopian government has become particularly important given the escalating operations in Blue Nile and their proximity to the Ethiopian border, which forms part of the wider security environment surrounding the fighting, the RSF source said. Developments in Blue Nile State were among the main issues on the table. The discussions covered troop movements along the border and cross-border security threats, the source said. The visit, they added, was part of ongoing political and security contacts with the Ethiopian government and broader outreach by the RSF leadership to Sudan’s neighboring countries. The Ethiopian government source said the discussions included the impact of continued fighting on Ethiopian areas bordering Sudan. They said Addis Ababa is looking to maintain open communication with Sudan’s various parties. Ethiopia’s immediate concern is to prevent the fighting from spilling over into its territory and to preserve stability in its border areas, the source added, particularly as military operations in Blue Nile have begun to directly affect neighboring Ethiopian areas. Addis Ababa, they added, is monitoring the movement of armed groups on both sides of the border. Armed fighters have repeatedly crossed the border in both directions in recent months. The RSF and the allied Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu have launched several major offensives in Blue Nile from across the border. The first came in March, when the two forces advanced on and captured the strategic town of Kurmuk, a key gateway between Blue Nile and Ethiopia. They launched another offensive in August, weeks after the military had retaken Kurmuk. Three military sources told Mada Masr last month that the August offensive, which reopened the fight over some of Blue Nile’s most strategically important border positions, was partly launched by forces that crossed from Asosa, located in Ethiopia’s Benishangul-Gumuz region, into Sudan. A local administrator in Asosa told Mada Masr at the time that heavy infantry units had been observed moving from an RSF base inside Ethiopia toward the Blue Nile border prior to the offensive. The movement has also gone in the opposite direction. In early August, a force of Tigrayan fighters crossed from Sudan into Western Tigray, an Ethiopian military source told Mada Masr at the time. Fighting subsequently broke out between the Ethiopian federal government and the TPLF , after four years of contentious peace between the two sides. Federal pressure on Tigray then escalated , followed by a surprising turn in alliances against Abiy. The renewed tensions with Tigray are part of how Sudan’s intelligence service understands Ethiopia’s interest in the RSF. The Ethiopian government could factor the paramilitary group into its military arrangements as it manages its conflicts with domestic opponents, particularly the TPLF, while gaining greater room to maneuver in Sudanese areas along its border, the intelligence source told Mada Masr. A closer Addis Ababa-RSF relationship is likely to register as a significant development for Tigray, particularly because of what it could mean for Western Tigray, the disputed area bordering Sudan, according to a former Sudanese diplomat informed of Ethiopia-Sudan relations. Tigrayan leaders are closely monitoring military and logistical movements along the border, the diplomat said, and a shift in the relationship could prompt them to reconsider their military posture there. The relationship could also serve Ethiopia in its dealings with Khartoum. It would give Addis Ababa a political and security channel to one of the main parties to Sudan’s war, which the government could use to exert pressure on Khartoum amid the diplomatic fallout between the two sides over Ethiopia’s increasing involvement in the war, the intelligence source said. For the military, that possibility carries particular weight as fighting continues in Blue Nile, where any security coordination between Addis Ababa and the RSF could affect how it manages the southeastern front, they added. What will determine the significance of Hemedti’s visit in the coming period is whether it is followed by security meetings or practical arrangements along the border, the former diplomat said. *** Buildup at Ethiopian base fuels concerns over RSF corridor toward Damazin A convoy of military vehicles moves through Ethiopia, April 27. Courtesy: Sudan Nabaa. A surge in military buildup at an Ethiopian military base in Asosa near the border with Sudan is raising concerns within the Sudanese military that the stretch of land between Asosa and RSF-held areas in Blue Nile could become a buffer zone entirely beyond the military’s attempts to reassert control, an intelligence source in the Fourth Infantry Division, based in Damazin, told Mada Masr. Such a zone could serve as an unimpeded corridor for supplies and military operations toward Damazin, the capital of Blue Nile, the source added. According to the source, the Sudanese military detected an increase in vehicles, ammunition and crates believed to contain weapons at the base, along with medical supplies intended for field hospitals. The Asosa base, located in Ethiopia’s Benishangul-Gumuz region and around 100 km from Blue Nile’s Kurmuk, belongs to the Ethiopian National Defense Forces, they added. Activity at the base had been visible since the start of the year but picked up in July, the source said, particularly as fighters from Darfur began arriving in Ethiopia via South Sudan. The flights ferrying them from South Sudan to Asosa, landing at dirt airstrips, have become so frequent that they are no longer especially discreet, the source added, noting that containers were also arriving at the base in greater numbers over the same period. The buildup has turned Asosa into a significant logistical hub, the source said, with implications for operations along the Blue Nile front. The scale of the buildup at the base was visible in satellite imagery. Yale’s Humanitarian Research Lab identified around 100 vehicles that arrived in the ENDF base between August 23 and 28, six times the number present at the site earlier. The new arrivals included vehicles with apparent mounted weapons and another group consistent with armored personnel carriers, as well as new vehicle carriers and trailers. Fifteen containers and eight cargo trucks were also identified. The surge came on top of an accumulation of materiel since late June, according to the lab’s report. The research lab identified at least 60 new cargo containers at the base between June 29 and August 23. The activity at Asosa was accompanied by an increase in cargo traffic from the United Arab Emirates, according to open-source flight-tracking data . The records show 46 flights by Ilyushin aircraft during August, with a notable increase in activity during the final week — the highest monthly total since the airbridge was established. A senior Ethiopian Air Force official told Mada Masr that the buildup serves both the federal government’s fight against domestic opponents and the RSF, but is primarily directed toward supporting the paramilitary group. The heightened activity at the base coincided with a major RSF and SPLM-N advance on the Blue Nile front in August, which began with the capture of Geisan and Kurmuk, which both sit near the Ethiopian border, and continued last week with attacks on military positions along the routes toward Damazin. The offensive on Geisan and Kurmuk was launched from across the border, according to the military sources who spoke to Mada Masr at the time. After withdrawing from Kurmuk in July, the RSF regrouped at camps in Asosa, one of the military sources said, adding that the fighters were reinforced with additional personnel, including mercenaries of various nationalities who had undergone advanced military training in the preceding weeks. On August 28, the RSF and its allies captured Bakori and Sirkum, with a military source saying the assault on Bakori was partly launched from inside Ethiopia. A Sudanese security source told Mada Masr that Asosa’s significance at this stage lies less in any declaration of Ethiopian involvement in the war and more in its geography. The base, they added, sits close to the Sudanese border and Asosa is linked by road and air routes that reach operational areas in Blue Nile. *** RSF moves on positions protecting Damazin, military sends for massive reinforcements RSF and SPLM-N troops are saluted after taking control of the Bakori and Sirkum areas in Blue Nile State, August 29. Courtesy: RSF. Two military positions in Blue Nile protecting the routes to the state capital Damazin fell to the RSF and its ally, the SPLM-N under Joseph Toka, on August 28. The military responded by moving reinforcements into Damazin and deploying additional forces and equipment toward the front. The RSF and its allies took control of Bakori in the Geisan locality and Sirkum in Kurmuk after battles that they described as “decisive.” Both areas had come under drone attacks in the preceding days. Last week, the military stated that it shot down a strategic drone over Sirkum it said had crossed the border from Ethiopia. The two positions are part of the network of military bases protecting Damazin. Bakori, about 170 km southeast of the state capital, is particularly significant, as it houses the headquarters of the military’s 14th Infantry Brigade, part of the Fourth Infantry Division based in Damazin. A military source told Mada Masr that the assault on Bakori was preceded by heavy attacks involving suicide and strategic drones as well as heavy artillery. The RSF and its allies then moved on the area on the morning of August 28 from three directions, including from inside Ethiopian territory and from Amora, north of the RSF-held town of Geisan, the source said. With the military lacking modern jamming systems capable of blunting the drone barrage, its forces eventually withdrew after fighting that lasted through the evening, abandoning the position and pulling back toward its northern outskirts, they added. After Bakori fell, the military also evacuated Sirkum, allowing the RSF and Toka’s forces to enter without a fight, according to the source. The RSF-led Tasis alliance, which heads the parallel government in western Sudan, said in a statement on the evening of August 28 that the operations represented a significant shift in the battlefield, adding that the military suffered heavy losses in personnel and equipment. A military source in the Fourth Infantry Division said that after the strategic border towns of Geisan and Kurmuk fell in mid-August, the battle had shifted farther from the border toward the positions protecting the routes to Damazin. Since the fall of Bakori and Sirkum last week, the military has sent substantial reinforcements from Khartoum, Gezira and Sennar states to Damazin, with the aim of retaking the towns and areas recently captured by the RSF in southeastern Blue Nile, a third military source told Mada Masr. The military has also moved a brigade from the elite forces of the General Intelligence Service toward the Bakori front, the source said. Additional battalions belonging to the joint force of armed movements allied with the military have also arrived in the area, according to the source. The forces are equipped with jamming systems, they said, and some have already begun deploying and preparing artillery and drone strikes against RSF positions from military defenses to the north of Bakori. For the Fourth Infantry Division source, however, the central problem facing the military is now supply rather than the initial loss of territory. Its forward units must simultaneously protect roads, supply depots, artillery positions and communications sites spread across large swaths of land. The geography favors a force able to operate along several axes, allowing the RSF and its allies operating from across the border and from SPLM-N territory, to pressure supply lines and force the military to redistribute its troops, the source said. The military, by contrast, relies on regular units and forces moving forward from Damazin, making any disruption to those lines of movement costly and complicating its ability to hold positions it recaptures, the source added. Burhan visited Damazin on Wednesday. Accompanied by Blue Nile’s governor and the commander of the Fourth Infantry Division, Burhan toured the city in an open-top vehicle, in an apparent effort to demonstrate the military’s control over the security situation and counter RSF claims that its forces are nearing Damazin. In a statement, the Fourth Infantry Division said Burhan inspected troops and assessed their combat readiness and preparedness to carry out their assigned duties. He was also briefed on the security and operational situation in the state. According to the statement, Burhan called for heightened readiness and vigilance, greater discipline and combat preparedness. *** Military captures new position in West Darfur; RSF fortifies Geneina with berms, reinforces troops The joint force of military-allied armed movements and mobilized civilian brigades captured Abu Sorug in West Darfur’s Sirba locality on Saturday. The area lies about 58 km from the RSF-held capital Geneina. The advance comes as the RSF reinforces its positions inside Geneina and builds earth berms around the city, while preparing its forces for attacks on military-held areas in West Darfur and neighboring North Darfur, according to a field source in the joint force. West Darfur Governor Bahr Eddin Karama said the military and its allies captured the Abu Sorug administrative unit after what he described as decisive fighting. The joint force field source told Mada Masr that its fighters advanced from Bir Saliba toward Abu Sorug, near the Chadian border, before clashing with RSF positions in the area. Bir Saliba, which sits about 30 km north of Geneina on the Sudan-Chad border, was captured by the military in July as part of an offensive launched from North Darfur that brought military and allied forces within reach of Geneina. The RSF has since launched several attacks in an effort to retake lost ground and ease pressure on the capital. The field source said the RSF gathered large numbers of fighters in Geneina this week in preparation for attacks on military positions in West Darfur and North Darfur. The group had paid salaries and incentives in advance to units assembled north and west of Geneina and supplied them with ammunition and other military provisions, the source said. The RSF has also been repositioning forces along the main roads leading toward military-held areas in Abu Sorug and Bir Saliba in West Darfur and Tina in North Darfur, according to the source. Inside Geneina, meanwhile, the RSF has shifted to a more defensive deployment, with earth berms extending across the city’s northern and western parts in anticipation of a possible surprise attack by the military, the source said. An RSF field source told Mada Masr during the July campaign that the group had begun digging trenches and building earth berms around the city’s outskirts. The RSF buildup has also extended to North Darfur. The Popular Resistance in North Darfur said the RSF gathered large numbers of fighters in the Ambro locality on Tuesday in preparation for an attack on the strategic border town of Tina. The following day, the group said, military aircraft carried out heavy strikes on the concentrations, scattering the forces and destroying a large number of vehicles. An activist in Tina told Mada Masr that a military drone also struck RSF gatherings on Wednesday in Um Marahik, in North Darfur’s Karnoi locality, destroying combat vehicles and sites used to store weapons and ammunition. *** Aerial attacks hit UN aid trucks, Dalang market in South Kordofan UN aid trucks after being struck by the RSF outside Dalang in South Kordofan, August 30. Courtesy: Motsim Jabr Aldar via Facebook. Two trucks carrying United Nations food aid to Kadugli were struck outside Dalang in South Kordofan on Sunday, days after an RSF drone attack on a market in the city killed three people and wounded others. The World Food Programme said the trucks were carrying food supplies and “were clearly marked with WFP banners and flags.” The attack destroyed more than 50 tons of food, “enough to provide lifesaving assistance to 5,800 people for one month,” the UN agency said. WFP described the attack as the latest example of the increasingly complex operating environment facing humanitarian organizations in Sudan. Since the beginning of the year, it said, WFP facilities have been affected by eight aerial attacks that damaged its premises and disrupted operations. Dalang itself came under an RSF drone attack on the evening of August 28, according to the Sudan Doctors Network. The strike hit a market and freight trucks near the city’s entrance, killing three people and wounding others. A community notable in Dalang told Mada Masr that the city has faced repeated RSF drone attacks over the preceding ten days. Most of the strikes have hit neighborhoods and areas where civilians gather, he said, adding that he believed the attacks were intended to force residents to leave. *** Military strikes RSF depots, concentrations in West Kordofan Military aircraft carried out strikes on Tuesday on RSF fuel and ammunition depots in Gafawa, northwest of Debeibat in West Kordofan, as well as on other RSF concentrations west of Khawi, a military source told Mada Masr. The strikes destroyed supplies that had reached RSF positions in the area earlier this week, the source said, describing the attacks as part of the military’s efforts to disrupt RSF supply routes and put pressure on its forces along the western axis. The attacks come as the military presses an offensive across Kordofan that has expanded since July. After rapidly advancing across North Kordofan and taking control of one of the RSF’s largest concentrations of fighters and military equipment in the region, the military now controls six of the state’s eight localities. It has since turned its attention westward, striking RSF positions in West Kordofan to lay the groundwork for an advance into the state. The RSF has repeatedly tried to claw back lost ground, launching attacks from both West Kordofan and its remaining positions in North Kordofan. An activist from North Kordofan’s Bara, captured by the military in July, told Mada Masr that RSF-affiliated groups attacked the Qaa and Kokeity areas west of the city on Saturday. The groups killed five young men and looted livestock and civilian homes, they said, prompting residents to flee and travel hundreds of kilometers toward western Omdurman in Khartoum. *** RSF commander in North Kordofan defects, arrives in capital with 200 fighters A group of RSF defectors arrive in Omdurman, August 30. Courtesy: Sudan News Agency A group of about 200 RSF fighters defected under Abu Bakr Dahloub, the paramilitary group’s intelligence chief for special missions in North Kordofan’s Hamra al-Sheikh and the Egypt-Libya-Sudan border triangle area and a member of its executive office. The defectors arrived in Omdurman on Sunday and announced that they were joining the military with their weapons and equipment. They said they were prepared to take part in combat operations alongside the military and allied forces. Speaking to the state-owned Sudan TV, Dahloub said the group had come to recognize what he called the mistake of joining “the statelet of evil” project carried out by the Dagalo family, and decided to side with what he described as the national camp and participate in operations against the RSF. Dahloub praised the efforts of former RSF leaders who recently defected to the military, naming former Darfur commanders Al-Nour “ Gubba ” Adam, Ali “ Savanna ” Rizgallah and Musa “ Khamseen ” Ahmed, among others. This is the second such defection by a senior field commander who held a command post on the Kordofan front — a decisive battleground and a critical faultline in the war. Former RSF field commander Hussein al-Dodo, who led one of the RSF’s units in Bara, arrived in Omdurman on July 22 with a force of 280 fighters, along with 30 fully equipped combat vehicles. During his interview, Dahloub alleged that Ilyushin aircraft were landing on dirt airstrips in North Kordofan’s Hamra al-Sheikh, each bringing eight-10 tons of weapons and ammunition and leaving with Sudanese goods. He said the continued flow of foreign weapons via these routes was helping prolong the war and called for identifying the sources of the RSF’s weapons and the parties behind its supply operations. *** Preparatory committee for state-led dialogue announced, outreach begins amid intractable disagreements Member of the preparatory committee for the state-led dialogue, journalist Osman Mirghani, speaks during a press conference organized by the committee in Khartoum, August 30. Courtesy: Sudan News Agency. The committee tasked with preparing the state-led political dialogue inside Sudan has moved from initial arrangements to outreach to political and civil forces, testing their willingness to participate and seeking initial understandings over some of the main objections to the process, according to two political sources informed of the committee’s work. The committee announced its formation at its first press conference in Khartoum on Sunday, naming Gasim Badry, the president of Ahfad University for Women, as its chair. It has 18 members, nine based inside Sudan and nine outside, including writer Al-Wathig Kameir, novelist Abdel Aziz Baraka Sakin and human rights lawyer Nabil Adeeb, alongside other academic, political and legal figures. The committee said its mandate was to prepare the ground for dialogue and engage with Sudanese political, civil and community forces. The state’s role, it said , should be limited to providing “guarantees, facilities and protection” without determining the participants, agenda or outcomes. Its first request was for the state to put into effect the legal guarantees Burhan had promised dialogue participants two weeks earlier, including temporary immunity and the suspension of criminal proceedings against those facing charges for the duration of their participation in the political process. The pledge was meant to clear a legal hurdle for several leaders of the opposition Sumud coalition, including its head, former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok, and others who were charged over what the military saw as their proximity to the RSF during the coalition’s earlier iteration as part of the Civil Front for Democracy. Justice Minister Abdallah Darf responded on Tuesday by announcing a decree from Burhan ordering the dismissal of complaints filed by state bodies against Sudanese nationals residing abroad who intend to enter Sudan to participate in the dialogue. The order also provides legal protection against prosecution for any statements, views or positions expressed during the sessions. The Transitional Sovereignty Council has yet to determine how long that protections will remain in effect after the dialogue ends, according to a judicial source at the Justice Ministry. With the legal guarantees now taking practical form, the committee is turning to the political work of bringing participants into the process. The most difficult issue at this stage is participation, a political source working as a communications advisor to the committee said. The potential field encompasses political and civil forces, armed movements, independent figures, social and professional groups and forces that have emerged during the war. Whether groups associated with ousted President Omar al-Bashir’s regime and the Islamist current should take part remains one of the most contentious questions, the source said. Committee member and journalist Osman Mirghani said at Sunday’s press conference that the intention was to position the body as a space that could rise above the polarization between Sudan’s political and military camps. But that ambition runs up against a narrower definition of participation set by Burhan himself. When he first announced the initiative in May, he said invitations would go to “national forces,” while excluding “those whose hands are stained with the blood of the Sudanese people,” effectively ruling out political forces aligned with the RSF. Several political forces opposed to the war collectively rejected the call for dialogue last week , at the conclusion of consultative meetings in Addis Ababa, arguing that a political process launched while fighting continues and control of the country remains divided would reflect the wartime balance of power rather than help end the war. The location of the dialogue is another point of contention. Civilian forces opposed to the war that left Sudan after fighting began argue that holding the process in military-controlled areas could distort the conditions for participation and undermine the dialogue’s independence, according to an informed source close to Hamdok. Asked by Mada Masr about the objection, Mirghani argued that holding the dialogue outside Sudan would “distance it from the communities that have borne the greatest burden of the war and diminish its political significance and ability to reflect the country’s reality.” A similar divide runs through the question of guarantees for the process itself. A political source in Sumud said the coalition remains unconvinced that the committee can operate independently of the government or provide guarantees for the dialogue’s independence, given that Burhan initiated the process himself. The source argued that a genuinely independent committee would have at least established its position toward the government before the state itself announced the initiative. Another long-standing faultline is over whether the dialogue should wait for an end to the fighting. Sumud has made a halt to the war and conditions for equal participation a prerequisite, while the committee sees the dialogue as something that can proceed in parallel with efforts to end the war, the source said. The committee’s outreach now is focused on resolving objections over participation, location and the body that will oversee the process before broader sessions begin, the two political sources informed of the outreach and the committee’s work said. For now, none of those questions has been settled. *** Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . The post Sudan Nashra: Hemedti in Addis Ababa | Buildup at Ethiopian base fuels concerns over RSF corridor toward Blue Nile capital, military sends massive reinforcements | RSF fortifies West Darfur capital with berms, reinforces troops | RSF commander in North Kordofan defects, arrives in capital with 200 fighters first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Hesson says Pakistan players used to 'chaos' after shake-up
items.description: Interim Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson hopes his drastically revamped squad can come through some all too familiar “chaos” with a much-improved showing against England in next week’s third and final Test in Birmingham. Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley, before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s on Sunday as England took an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-match campaign. The Pakistan Cricket Board responded to those defeats in dramatic fashion, taking the extraordinary step of sending seven players home, calling up another seven and replacing sacked Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, already Pakistan’s white-ball boss. Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha — Pakistan’s captain at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured — were among those told to leave. Left-arm spin bowler Ali Usman, who claimed a five-wicket haul at Headingley, and seamer Khurram Shahzad were also sent home. Of the seven replacements, only batsmen Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience. Hesson, however, feels the whole squad can now unite and give a better account of themselves when the third Test at Edgbaston starts on September 9. The New Zealander had recently been in Japan preparing for the Asian Games and was only due to travel to the UK for the squad’s audience with King Charles, which took place on Wednesday. “I was heading over to see the King and be part of a nice occasion. That got expedited,” Hesson told reporters at Edgbaston on Friday, as quoted by the BBC . “The last couple of days have been challenging for being in a hotel with some players coming, some players going and then the arrival of everyone. “The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. There is no doubt they have been disappointed, incredibly disappointed. We have had to park that and go ‘righto, where to from here?’ They have been really good over the past couple of days.” Hesson added: “I don’t think anyone wants this to happen in the middle of a series. “From my perspective, it is about putting a balanced squad together, not only for this Test, so we actually have some variety in our attack,” he adds. “Pakistan is known for the pace, unusual actions, mystery spin — we haven’t really been able to present any of that.”

items.title: Volkswagen board approves plan to cut another 50,000 jobs
items.description: The board of German car giant Volkswagen has approved a plan to cut another 50,000 jobs as part of the biggest restructuring in the group’s almost nine-decade history. It brings the total number of roles the carmaker plans to shed by 2030 to 100,000, after announcing in March that it would cut 50,000 roles. The group – which includes Audi, Porsche, Skoda as well as the VW brand – is also considering the future of four of its German plants. The move is a “strong signal” for the future of the firm, which is “taking responsibility for our entire workforce”, VW’s chief executive Oliver Blume said in a statement on Thursday. Blume said in July that the firm was looking to make the additional cuts. Shares in the company were up by around 7% in Frankfurt on Friday morning. The Golf-maker has been hit by a drop in profits due to falling sales and fierce competition, especially from Chinese brands. The firm also said that by 2035 it would cut the number of models it produces by 50% and reduce the complexity of its offering by 75%. VW will also prioritise the “most compelling vehicles” and make more of each model, which will help lower costs, it said. A “fundamental adjustment of the global workforce capability is necessary” to safeguard the competitiveness of the company, which faces shifting demand and technological change. It added “a group-wide workforce adjustment of approximately 50,000 positions – including management roles – will be necessary.” The company is also weighing options for operations in Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Neckarsulm, where it has said production capacity exceeds demand. “Alternative uses for these plants are being assessed,” it said. As of 2025, VW employed more than 660,000 people worldwide. Its brands also include Seat, Bentley and Lamborghini. Christianne Benner – the president of Europe’s largest industrial union IG Metall and deputy chair of VW’s Supervisory Board – said the carmaker had “fought hard for good solutions” to address a “crisis situation”. VW’s profits have fallen sharply in recent years, hit by falling sales in China, which was once one of its biggest markets. Sales have also fallen in the US, partly due to the impact of tariffs on car imports that were introduced by President Donald Trump’s administration. Chinese carmakers have been expanding aggressively as they roll out new technologies while benefiting from lower production costs than their rivals. In recent years, firms such as BYD have seen their sales rise sharply in markets including the UK, European Union and South East Asia.

items.title: Pêche au poulpe : l'éclairage du Secrétariat d’État sur les mesures de protection
items.description: La Secrétairerie d’État chargée de la Pêche maritime a réagi aux déclarations et informations récemment relayées au sujet de la pêche au poulpe, dénonçant des « allégations erronées » qui remettraient en cause la manière dont cette activité est encadrée. Dans un communiqué, le Département affirme que les décisions régissant le secteur reposent sur les données scientifiques et les avis techniques de l’Institut national de recherche halieutique (INRH). L’objectif affiché est de préserver les ressources marines et d’éviter leur surexploitation, tout en tenant compte des équilibres sociaux et économiques du secteur. S’agissant spécifiquement du poulpe, le Secrétariat d’État rappelle plusieurs mesures récemment adoptées pour protéger les juvéniles et les zones de reproduction. Le décret ministériel n°08/2026, daté du 17 août, prévoit ainsi la fermeture de la zone dite des « petits poulpes » , au sud de Sidi El Ghazi, notamment au sud du 22°42’ de latitude Nord. Un second texte, le décret n°10/2026 du 27 août, a par ailleurs modifié les dispositions du décret n°05/2026 du 29 juin. Il prévoit l’interdiction du chalutage de fond, sur une bande maritime située entre les latitudes 26°24’ Nord et 22°42’ Nord, à 18 milles nautiques des côtes, du 28 août au 10 septembre 2026. À compter du 10 septembre, l’activité de chalutage devra être totalement suspendue dans la zone concernée. Le Secrétariat d’État explique que la période de repos biologique devait initialement débuter le 16 septembre. Mais après l’observation, dans les captures, d’une forte présence de juvéniles de poulpe, dépassant 60%, l’INRH avait recommandé d’avancer l’arrêt de la pêche au 1er septembre. La date a finalement été reportée au 10 septembre afin de tenir compte des considérations socio-économiques et des demandes des professionnels. L’administration assure également qu’aucune décision n’a été prise dans le but d’accorder à une partie ou à des individus des ressources financières ou des avantages susceptibles d’être utilisés à des fins partisanes ou électorales. Elle affirme que la gestion des ressources halieutiques nationales repose exclusivement sur les évaluations scientifiques, l’intérêt national et les orientations du plan Halieutis et de la feuille de route 2025-2027. Le Secrétariat d’État réaffirme enfin que l’octroi des licences et les décisions administratives dans le secteur sont soumis aux lois et règlements en vigueur, sur la base de critères objectifs et de procédures institutionnelles, « sans aucune considération politique, partisane ou électorale ». items.title: Police arrest mother and son over suspected drugs in Dormaa Ahenkro
items.description: The Bono Regional Drug Law Enforcement Unit has arrested a 66-year-old woman and her 29-year-old son for allegedly possessing suspected narcotic and restricted drugs at Kumi Daa Street (KDS), a suburb of the Dormaa Central Municipality in the Bono Region. According to a press release issued on Friday, September 4, the suspects, identified as Mary Awuni and her son, Maxwell Akukah, were arrested during an intelligence-led operation, according to the Bono Regional Police Command. A search of their rooms resulted in the recovery of 147 yellow compressed slabs wrapped in sellotape, suspected to be Indian hemp, as well as 270 boxes and 329 blisters of assorted Tramadol. The Police also recovered 14 blisters of Rohypnol, GH¢87,751 and CFA 2,000 during the operation. According to the Police, Mrs Awuni was found with a metal trunk containing the 14 blisters of Rohypnol, GH¢72,612 and CFA 2,000. During questioning, she reportedly claimed that the items and money had been given to her by a man in Accra for delivery to another person in Côte d’Ivoire. The Police, however, said Mrs Awuni admitted ownership of the items found in her room. Her son, Maxwell Akukah, was arrested in a separate room where the suspected Indian hemp, Tramadol and GH¢15,139 were found. Mr Akukah reportedly told investigators that the items belonged to his brother, Anthony, who was said to be outside Dormaa Ahenkro at the time of the operation. The two suspects are currently in Police custody assisting with investigations as the Bono Regional Police Command works to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged possession of the substances. The Police said investigations are ongoing towards the prosecution of persons found culpable. The Command has also reaffirmed its commitment to tackling narcotics-related offences in the region and urged members of the public to provide credible information to assist law enforcement agencies. It said public cooperation was essential to helping the Police protect communities and maintain public safety.

items.title: NSMQ 2026: Inside the profiles of this year’s three grand finalists chasing glory
items.description: The 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) grand finale will bring together three schools with vastly different histories in Ghana’s biggest academic competition. Record holders Presbyterian Boys’ Secondary School (PRESEC-Legon), two-time champions St Augustine’s College and debutants Accra Academy will battle for the coveted trophy and the ultimate bragging rights after surviving intense competition to emerge as this year’s finalists. While PRESEC-Legon arrives with a rich history of dominance, St Augustine’s College brings championship experience and recent consistency to the contest. Accra Academy, on the other hand, enters the final with an opportunity to make history in its maiden appearance on the competition’s biggest stage. Here is a look at the profiles of the three finalists. PRESEC-Legon: The record holders Presbyterian Boys’ Secondary School, popularly known as PRESEC-Legon or Ɔdadeɛ, heads into the 2026 final as the most successful school in the history of the National Science and Maths Quiz. The Legon-based school has won the competition a record eight times, lifting the trophy in 1995, 2003, 2006, 2008, 2009, 2020, 2022 and 2023. PRESEC has also made an impressive 13 appearances at the grand finale and finished as first runner-up on four occasions. The school holds another remarkable record as the only institution to have won the NSMQ back-to-back on two separate occasions. The ‘Ɔdadeɛ’ boys successfully defended their title in 2009 after winning in 2008 and repeated the feat by winning consecutive titles in 2022 and 2023. Guided by the motto, “In Lumine Tuo Videbimus Lumen,” meaning “In Thy Light We Shall See Light,” PRESEC-Legon will enter the 2026 final with its sights firmly set on extending its record with a historic ninth trophy. St Augustine’s College: The two-time champions St Augustine’s College, popularly known as AUGUSCO, is no stranger to the grand stage. The Cape Coast-based school has won the National Science and Maths Quiz twice, emerging champions in 2007 and 2019. The 2026 final will mark AUGUSCO’s fifth appearance at the grand finale, having previously reached the decisive contest in 2007, 2019, 2024 and 2025. Apart from its two championship triumphs, the school has also finished as first runner-up on one occasion and second runner-up once. AUGUSCO also boasts continental credentials as champions of the West Africa NSMQ. The school heads into this year’s contest with recent experience on its side, having now reached the grand finale for three consecutive years – 2024, 2025 and 2026. With its motto, “Omnia Vincit Labour,” meaning “Perseverance Conquers All,” AUGUSCO will be hoping perseverance carries it to a third national title. Accra Academy: The history makers For Accra Academy, the 2026 NSMQ grand finale represents a historic breakthrough. Known affectionately as Blɛoo, the school will make its first-ever appearance at the grand finale of the competition. The journey to this stage has already made the 2026 campaign one of the most memorable in Accra Academy’s NSMQ history. The school had previously reached the semi-finals in 2020 but fell short of a place in the final. Six years later, Blɛoo has gone one step further. Now, Accra Academy has the opportunity to transform its maiden appearance at the grand finale into an even bigger piece of history by winning its first-ever NSMQ trophy. Guided by the motto, “Esse Quam Videri,” meaning “To Be Rather Than To Seem,” the school will enter the contest as the only debutant among the finalists. One final, three different stories The 2026 NSMQ grand finale, scheduled for Thursday, September 10, promises to be a fascinating clash of pedigree, experience and ambition. PRESEC-Legon will be chasing history and a record-extending ninth title. St Augustine’s College will be seeking to add a third championship to its collection and return to the summit for the first time since 2019. Accra Academy will be hoping to crown its maiden appearance at the grand finale with an unforgettable first trophy. Whatever happens, the 2026 final will produce another chapter in the rich history of the National Science and Maths Quiz. For one school, however, the night will end with the ultimate prize. The 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz is produced by Primetime Limited and sponsored by the Ghana Education Service with support from GOIL PLC, Prudential Life Insurance Ghana, Pepsodent, Cowbell, Trustur AI and Jupay Money Transfer. The Broadcast on JoyNews is sponsored by Vitamilk, Entrance University of Health Sciences, Chartered Institute of Management Accountants and NASCO.
